text: Correct: k⟮α⟯ contains its own transcendental generator, and adjoining that generator over k recovers the whole intermediate field. The remaining extension therefore has degree one, exactly [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.1](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean uses the subtype generator and transports its transcendence through the injective inclusion into E. The ambient E need not itself be a function field or be finite over k(α). The published native RatFunc construction provides the same degree-one parameter model. No canonical identification of all transcendental generators is asserted. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L121).
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.

Correct: if F has transcendence degree one over both k and the embedded k′, the [tower formula](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/030H) forces trdegₖ(k′)=0, hence k′/k is algebraic. The compatible tower is explicit. Lean does not infer algebraicity merely because k′ lies inside F: the second function-field hypothesis is essential. The source proves the cardinal-rank implication, including the finite value one. The published C(x)/R control and native C(x)/C construction realize two legitimate bases without falsely requiring them to coincide or be exact. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L251).
The source constructs the genuine non-exact extension C(x)/R as a function field and computes ℓ(0)=2; exact constants cannot be inferred.
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.

Correct: restricting constants from k′ to k preserves a function field when k′/k is finite. Finite generation composes in the tower, while algebraic base change preserves transcendence degree one. This is the finite-tower consequence of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.1](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The finite-degree hypothesis prevents an infinite constant extension from being mistaken for a finitely generated field over k. The published [C(x)/R calculation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/RealComplex.lean#L28) actually invokes this theorem using [C:R]=2 and obtains ℓ(0)=2, so exact constants are correctly absent. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L268).
The source constructs the genuine non-exact extension C(x)/R as a function field and computes ℓ(0)=2; exact constants cannot be inferred.

Correct: an algebraic intermediate constant extension k′/k contributes no transcendence degree, and finite field generation over k remains finite over k′. Thus the same F is a function field over k′, as in [Stichtenoth, Corollary 1.1.16 and the normalization of constants preceding Section 1.4](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean requires k′ to embed compatibly inside F; this is not a claim about an arbitrary tensor product or compositum. Native C(x) over R and over C supplies the existing non-exact-constants control. No separability or exact-constants condition is introduced. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L257).
The source constructs the genuine non-exact extension C(x)/R as a function field and computes ℓ(0)=2; exact constants cannot be inferred.
The actual rational-function object supplies transcendental X and finite degree over its generated intermediate field.

Correct: degree one means the constants map onto the residue field; equivalently every regular f differs from some constant by an element of the maximal ideal. This is rational-place evaluation in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean uses v(f−c)<1, which includes exact equality f=c because v(0)=0; replacing it by positive ord without a zero guard would be wrong. The published infinity evaluation computes the constant from the leading coefficients and handles zero separately. Infinite residue dimension cannot masquerade as degree one. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L532).
The published rational-function computation supplies a constant residue at infinity, including zero and negative-degree functions.
The source proves degree one for the native infinity place using the actual constant-residue calculation.

Correct: a residue field algebraic over algebraically closed k equals k through its constants embedding, so its k-dimension is one. This matches [Stichtenoth, Remark 1.1.17](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean's `Algebra.IsIntegral` is equivalent to algebraicity over a field and supplies the necessary restriction: an arbitrary transcendental residue extension need not collapse. No function-field assumption is needed once residue algebraicity is given. The native infinity residue computation is already degree one over every field, providing the concrete rational-place control without adding an unproved specialization. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L574).
The source proves degree one for the native infinity place using the actual constant-residue calculation.

Correct: equivalent valuations induce the same order comparisons, and surjectivity onto the fixed discrete value group fixes their normalization. They therefore agree as valuations and define the same place, matching [Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.1.13](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Without normalization, rescaling would preserve equivalence but not numerical values. Both places carry that surjectivity in their structure. The published valuation-ring injectivity theorem genuinely uses this result; the native X-membership calculation distinguishes infinity from finite places. No arbitrary uniformizer choices need to agree. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L431).
The existing valuation-ring comparison reduces equal rings to equivalent normalized valuations and applies this theorem.
The actual rational coordinate is outside the valuation ring precisely at infinity, checking the regular/pole distinction.

Correct: surjectivity of the normalized valuation supplies an element of value exp(−1), hence a uniformizer. This is the prime-element existence in [Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.1.6](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean's place already contains discreteness and nontrivial normalization, so no global function-field hypothesis is needed. The witness cannot be zero, whose value is zero rather than a group generator. The published native infinity place explicitly uses X⁻¹ as its uniformizer and computes order one, testing the precise sign and normalization of the existence claim. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L390).
The existing native infinity place has the explicit uniformizer X⁻¹, with its normalized order computed in the proof.
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.

Correct: choose a nonzero coefficient of least order; every ratio then has nonnegative order and lies in O(P), while its own ratio is one. The finite index type and supplied nonzero entry ensure that minimum exists; zero coefficients are handled separately. This uses the valuation-ring criterion in [Stacks, Section 10.50](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I8). The published residue-extension proof actually applies this normalization to minimal-polynomial coefficients. [Target provenance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/commit/f42e3235f2d059110cea3c8604b2f2ddc97af07c) identifies the publishing account as an author of this implementation. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L298).
The published proof normalizes the finite coefficient family of a minimal polynomial using this exact theorem before reducing it to a nonzero residue polynomial.

Correct: a surjective valuation with integer value group has a discrete valuation ring as its valuation subring, matching [Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.1.6](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean's instance applies the normalized-valuation API to the actual P.integers carrier. Surjectivity excludes a field with trivial valuation and supplies a nonunit generator; no separate noetherian hypothesis is being silently assumed. The published prime-element decomposition writes every nonzero field element as tⁿ times a valuation-ring unit. At the native infinity place, X⁻¹ is the explicit generator. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L371).
The source proves the actual nonzero-element decomposition into an integer power of a uniformizer times a unit of P.integers.
The existing native infinity place has the explicit uniformizer X⁻¹, with its normalized order computed in the proof.

Correct: a uniformizer has normalized additive order one, exactly the prime-element convention in [Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.1.6 and Definition 1.1.12](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The source identifies Mathlib's discrete value-group generator with exp(−1), so the equivalence uses +1 rather than −1. No nonzero premise is missing: either side excludes zero because ord(0)=0 and zero cannot generate the nonzero value group. Both sides are directly verified for the published X⁻¹ uniformizer at infinity. The theorem does not select a unique uniformizer. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L383).
The existing native infinity place has the explicit uniformizer X⁻¹, with its normalized order computed in the proof.
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.

Correct: an element of the valuation ring is invertible there exactly when its valuation is one, the unit criterion in [Stacks, Lemma 10.50.16](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I8). Lean quantifies over x:P.integers, so membership is built into its type; an inverse in F alone would not suffice. Zero fails both sides without an extra guard. The adjoining maximal-ideal theorem uses v(x)<1, giving the complementary nonunit case. The explicit infinity uniformizer has order one, hence lies in the nonunit part rather than the unit group. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L393).
The existing maximal-ideal characterization uses strict valuation less than one, complementary to the unit equality.
The existing native infinity place has the explicit uniformizer X⁻¹, with its normalized order computed in the proof.

Correct: regularity at P is nonnegative additive order, the valuation-ring description in [Stacks, Lemma 10.50.16](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I8). Lean's totalized ord assigns zero to f=0, and this particular equivalence remains valid there because zero belongs to the ring. For nonzero f the result is v(f)≤1 rewritten through exp(−ord(f)); the inequality direction is correct. The native X-membership theorem excludes exactly infinity, and X⁻¹ has positive order there. The equivalence is not incorrectly extended to positive order as a zero-input maximal-ideal criterion. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L256).
The actual rational coordinate is outside the valuation ring precisely at infinity, checking the regular/pole distinction.
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.

Correct: the residue field is a nonzero k-vector space, so finite dimension is at least one. This is the positivity implicit in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14 and Proposition 1.1.15](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean explicitly requires `Module.Finite k P.ResidueField`; without it, `finrank` could return zero for an infinite-dimensional extension. The hypothesis is local residue finiteness, weaker than requiring a whole function-field structure. Published infinity and X²+1 computations give actual degrees one and two, respectively, checking that the invariant measures residue degree rather than counting places. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L521).
The source proves degree one for the native infinity place using the actual constant-residue calculation.
The explicitly constructed irreducible X²+1 place has residue degree two, providing the nonrational boundary control.

Correct: this is the valuation homomorphism Fˣ→Z, expressed with Lean's additivized unit group. Multiplication of functions becomes addition in the domain, and `ord_mul` supplies the homomorphism law. Restricting to units excludes the junk value ord(0)=0. This matches the valuation laws underlying [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.12](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The published application equation and principal-divisor order-system equation identify the actual map used downstream. [Target provenance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/commit/55e7ba367b37e6d812ce9a1b0ef349d359a371ed) identifies the publishing account as an author of this implementation. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L192).
The existing defining equation identifies the map on a genuine field unit with its order.
The published divisor order-system API uses this exact homomorphism and recovers the actual order of each unit.

Correct: a place is trivial on nonzero constants, so their multiplicative valuation is one and their additive order is zero. This is the constant-field convention in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.9](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean also includes c=0, using its explicitly documented totalization ord(0)=0 rather than applying the nonzero triviality axiom. No exact-constants assumption is required. The published order formula for cXᵃ(X−1)ᵇ actually uses this constant contribution while retaining c≠0 for the surrounding multiplication laws; thus zero is not silently treated as a multiplicative unit. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L315).
The actual rational-function family cXᵃ(X−1)ᵇ has order −(a+b) at infinity for nonzero c.

Correct: every nonzero element algebraic over k belongs, together with its inverse, to each valuation ring trivial on k; its valuation is therefore one and its order zero. This is the enlarged-constant-field behavior in [Stichtenoth, Proposition 1.1.5(c)](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean handles zero separately with ord(0)=0. Consequently the statement requires neither exact constants nor a global function-field assumption. The published transcendence criterion genuinely takes its contrapositive, and the native C(x)/R example confirms why algebraic constants beyond R must not be classified as zeros or poles. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L331).
The existing contrapositive excludes algebraic elements from nonzero order, including nonexact constants.
The source constructs the genuine non-exact extension C(x)/R as a function field and computes ℓ(0)=2; exact constants cannot be inferred.

Correct: orders add under multiplication of nonzero functions, matching the discrete valuation law in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.9](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Both nonzero guards are essential for Lean's Z-valued totalization: with f=0, the conclusion would incorrectly force ord(g)=0. In a field they also ensure fg≠0. The published native family cXᵃ(X−1)ᵇ computes order −(a+b) at infinity using this law, with its coefficient nonvanishing retained. Constants, units, and poles follow the same normalization; there is no extra assumption on characteristic or function-field finiteness. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L171).
The actual rational-function family cXᵃ(X−1)ᵇ has order −(a+b) at infinity for nonzero c.

Correct: in any finite nontrivial linear relation, nonzero scalar coefficients have order zero; injectively distinct orders leave a unique least-order summand, which cannot cancel. This is the strict triangle principle of [Stichtenoth, Lemma 1.1.11](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean allows an arbitrary index type because linear independence tests finite relations. The explicit nonzero-family hypothesis excludes the false singleton-zero case. The published Weierstrass-coordinate proof applies this theorem to the six actual monomials 1,x,y,x²,xy,x³ and computes their distinct orders 0,−2,−3,−4,−5,−6 in its source. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L287).
The existing source computes the six monomial orders and uses linearIndependent_of_injective_ord to prove their independence before deriving the Weierstrass relation.

Correct: if f has two constant residues a and b, subtracting the two errors gives a constant of valuation below one. A nonzero constant has value one, forcing a=b. This is uniqueness of the residue value in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean uses strict multiplicative inequalities, so exact equality f=a is included without an ord(0) error. It needs neither f to be explicitly regular nor the place to have degree one: the hypotheses themselves give two constant residues. The published infinity calculation supplies such residues concretely. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L350).
The published rational-function computation supplies a constant residue at infinity, including zero and negative-degree functions.
The published infinity computation identifies the residue of a nonzero degree-zero rational function with the numerator/denominator leading-coefficient ratio.

Hom_C(Cₙ(X;R),M), with coboundary given by precomposition with ∂, is exactly the exposed `linearYonedaObj` value. For C=ModuleCat k and R=k this is ordinary M-valued singular cochains, as in [Hatcher §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=206). The more general R and C are explicitly documented; no reflexivity or finite-support condition on cochains is inserted. The published differential and pullback evaluation lemmas confirm the direction and signs. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/Basic.lean#L92).
Published equation δf=f∘∂, including the grading reversal.
Published pullback evaluation fixes the contravariant convention.

The `.homology n` of this ℕ-indexed cochain complex is ker(δⁿ)/im(δⁿ⁻¹), with degree zero unreduced. That matches [Hatcher §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=206) after taking C=ModuleCat k and R=k. For general coefficient object R, the docstring accurately says cohomology of Hom(C(X;R),M). The existing identity/composition theorems confirm that continuous maps induce contravariant cohomology maps; there is no unsupported UCT or duality identification. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/Basic.lean#L127).
Published identity law on the actual cohomology object.
Published contravariant composition law.

The isomorphism sends a base cochain f to c↦f(p_*c); its inverse descends a G-invariant cochain. Both evaluations are proved in the published source. `IsQuotientCoveringMap` supplies surjectivity, free fibres and simplex lifting, so no averaging or invertibility of |G| is needed. The differential is precomposition with boundary, and p_* commutes with boundary. This is Hom_G(C(E;k),M) with trivial M, consistent with [Brown §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=13); contractibility is correctly unnecessary at this chain level. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/GroupCohomology.lean#L105).
Published comparison evaluates to f(p_*c).
Published inverse evaluates on p_*c as f(c).

For a quotient covering with contractible total space, C(E;k) is a projective resolution of trivial k. Applying Hom_G(-,M), with trivial M, and the actual pullback cochain isomorphism gives the displayed Hⁿ(B;M)≅Hⁿ(G,M). This agrees with [Brown §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=13). The source uses `groupCohomologyIso` in the correct direction; degree zero is included, and neither finiteness of G nor a characteristic restriction is assumed. The published forward/inverse cochain formulas fix which comparison induces this isomorphism. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/GroupCohomology.lean#L169).
Published chain-level pullback formula for the comparison used here.
Published exactness of the augmentation of the actual equivariant singular chain complex.

An element g acts by pushing chains along x↦g•x. The proof of `map_mul` composes h then g, giving the direct left action ρ(gh)=ρ(g)ρ(h), and the simplex formula preserves coefficients. This is the chain-action construction underlying [Brown §1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=4), extended here to monoids by functoriality. Freeness and contractibility are correctly absent from this definition; continuous translation is sufficient. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Resolution.lean#L71).
Published translation-chain-map equation.
Published action on every simplex and coefficient.

The equality identifies ρ(g) with the degree-n linear map induced by translation x↦g•x. Its right side has exactly the same domain and codomain as the representation action; it does not use g⁻¹. The published simplex-action theorem confirms this orientation. It exposes the chain action used in [Brown §1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=4), and remains valid for continuous monoid actions without freeness or contractibility. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Resolution.lean#L92).
Published coefficient-preserving basis action checks the same translation convention.

The formula ρ(g)(aσ)=a(g•σ) is the expected linear action on the singular-simplex basis. The coefficient a is unchanged and the translated simplex uses direct left translation. The proof reduces to the published pushforward formula and the pointwise simplex action, matching the chain-action convention in [Brown §1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=4). It covers a=0 and degree zero without additional hypotheses. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Resolution.lean#L98).
Published general pushforward formula specialized by the proof.

The underlying linear map is ∂:Cₙ₊₁(E;k)→Cₙ(E;k). Its intertwining field is the chain-map identity for each translation, so it is genuinely a morphism of representations. The published evaluation lemma and alternating-face formula preserve the ordinary singular boundary signs. This is the equivariant chain differential in [Brown §1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=4); no free action is needed merely to make ∂ equivariant. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Resolution.lean#L109).
Published underlying-boundary evaluation.
Published alternating-face boundary formula.

For every chain c in degree n+1, forgetting equivariance from `singularChainsRepDifferential` gives exactly the native singular boundary applied to c. The indices agree, including n=0, and no sign or conjugation is inserted. Together with the published alternating-face formula, this identifies the boundary convention used by the equivariant complex in [Brown §1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=4). [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Resolution.lean#L118).
Published boundary on simplex generators.

The complex has Cₙ(E;k) with the direct G-action in degree n, and the ordinary singular boundary as differential. `ChainComplex.of` uses the existing ∂²=0 identity; the published degree and differential equations expose these choices. This is the chain complex of representations underlying [Brown §1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=4). It is not yet asserted to be exact or projective: those properties require the additional hypotheses appearing later. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Resolution.lean#L124).
Published identification of each term.
Published identification of each boundary.

The successor differential of `singularChainsRep` equals `singularChainsRepDifferential` with the same n. Thus forgetting the representation gives ∂:Cₙ₊₁→Cₙ, with the native alternating-face convention. This is the boundary in the equivariant chain complex described in [Brown §1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=4). The statement does not misidentify unrelated degree pairs or claim exactness. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Resolution.lean#L144).

After forgetting G, this isomorphism is the identity in every chain degree. The equivariant differential forgets to the original boundary, so the identity components commute with it.
